villages.traditional_livestock_practices: 5.5 Traditional Knowledge & Customary Practices Surrounding Livestock Keeping Practice Relevance ● Free-Range System ● Chickens are allowed to roam freely, foraging for food and water. ● Traditional Feeding Practices ● Chickens are mostly fed a diet of rice and maize. ● Ethno- Veterinary Practices ● Traditional healers use local herbs like Pine leaves, fishmints, peach to treat chicken ailments. ● Pig Rearing ● Pigs are reared in traditional enclosures, made from bamboo and thatch or tin, timber, cement concrete which results in a low incidence of diseases and clean sty. ● Diet ● Pigs are fed a diet of rice, forest leaves, maize and powdered rice husk. ● Breeding and training ● The local dogs are trained by the villagers for hunting, guarding and companionship. ● Healthcare ● The villagers use local herbs and medicines to treat dog ailments. ● Diet ● Dogs are fed a diet of rice, meat and vegetables. . ● Companionship ● Cats are kept as companions and are often pampered by their owners and are fed with rice, meat and milk. ● Healthcare ● Locals use fermented fish, tinfish and cooked sticky flavored rice to treat cat diseases.

Dzukhaori: The Community Pond This traditional community pond has played a pivotal role in the village's development and daily life. As the village's first water source, it has been a vital component of the community's existence. Historically, the water from this pond was used for various ritual purposes performed by the villagers, underscoring its significance in their spiritual lives. The pond's importance extends beyond its practical uses, as it has become an integral part of the village's cultural heritage. 2. Muzedu: The Natural Salty Spring Well Muzedu, a natural salty spring well, serves as a drinking source for animals. This unique water body is not only a vital resource for the village's fauna but also a fascinating example of the region's geological characteristics. 3. Chokholo Muze: The Mythical Pond Chokholo Muze, a mystical pond, is steeped in local legend. According to tradition, only a fortunate individual from the village can discover the rare and exquisite white Angel trumpet flower, which is said to bloom in this enchanted pond. This myth has contributed to the pond's allure, making it a revered and sought-after destination for villagers and visitors alike.

Rafühao: The Devil's Domain Rafühao, a foreboding area, has long been feared by the locals, who believe it to be a place of dark forces. According to legend, anyone who ventures into this area never returns, leaving behind only whispers of terror and unease. The villagers' deep-seated fear of Rafühao has led to its avoidance, with many considering it a place best left unexplored. 2. Zuvüri River: The Abode of Satan The ancient villagers believed that the Zuvüri River was home to Satan himself, striking fear into the hearts of all who dared to approach its waters. This dark reputation has persisted, with many locals continuing to view the river with a mix of trepidation and awe. 3. Khazi pü ngaonuoze Lake: The Living snake lake The Khazi pü ngaonuoze Lake was once said to be home to a fearsome snake, a creature so terrifying that it was believed to be a ghost. According to local legend, Mamaso (which means ghost in Tsupfume dialect) would often emerge from the depths of the lake to frighten unsuspecting villagers. However, the snake's reign of terror eventually came to an end when brave villagers banded together to kill the beast. With Mamaso vanquished, the lake is now safe for villagers to cross, although the legend of the ghostly snake continues to captivate and unsettle all who hear it. 4.
